# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. Cell Coloring & Shading
Games where cells are marked as filled/shaded or empty based on logical constraints.

### A. Pure Shading
- Akari (light bulbs and dark cells)
- Hitori (eliminate duplicate cells)
- Kurodoko (black cells block visibility)
- Kurotto (black cells around numbered clues)
- Nurikabe (black/white regions with number clues)
- Nuritwin (paired black regions)
- Nurimisaki (black regions with cape endpoints)
- Satogaeri (return to village with shading)
- Sto-stone (stone placement with shading)
- Usowan (truth/lie cells)

### B. Shading with Polyomino Constraints
- LITS (tetrominoes in regions)
- Norinori (three-cell polyominoes per region)
- Shakashaka (triangular shading in cells)
- Shikaku (rectangular regions)

### C. Shading with Path/Connectivity
- Heyawake (shaded regions with path constraints)
- Makaro (shaded regions with connectivity)
- Nurimeizu (shaded maze-like regions)

## II. Path & Loop Drawing
Games where continuous lines or paths are drawn on the grid.

### A. Single Closed Loop
- Dotchi-Loop (loop with dot constraints)
- Hebi (snake loop)
- Masyu (loop through pearls and circles)
- Mid-loop (loop with midpoint constraints)
- Slitherlink (loop around grid edges)

### B. Multiple Paths/Connections
- Hashiwokakero (bridges between islands)
- Numberlink (connecting matching numbers)
- Sashigane (L-shaped paths)
- Suraromu (spiral paths)

### C. Path with Shading Integration
- Nagareru (flowing paths with shading)
- Ripple Effect (rippling paths in regions)
- Yajilin (path with shaded obstacles)

## III. Region & Polyomino Placement
Games focused on dividing the grid into specific shapes or regions.

### A. Polyomino Tiling
- Chained Block (connected blocks)
- Evolomino (evolving polyominoes)
- Fillomino (polyominoes matching size numbers)
- Five Cells (five-cell regions)

### B. Chocolate/Candy Themed
- Choco Banana (chocolate piece placement)
- Double Choco (paired chocolate regions)

### C. Region Division with Constraints
- Tilepaint (tiling with color constraints)
- Yosenabe (region grouping)

## IV. Constraint Satisfaction & Deduction
Games based on logical deduction with numerical or symbolic constraints.

### A. Sudoku Family
- Sudoku (standard number placement)
- Juosan (number placement variant)
- Nansuke (number placement variant)

### B. Visibility & Blocking
- Moon-or-Sun (celestial object placement)
- Pencils (pencil placement with visibility)

## V. Hybrid/Multi-Mechanic Games
Games combining multiple core mechanics.

- Kurodoko (shading + visibility)
- Norinori (shading + polyominoes)
- Satogaeri (shading + path logic)

---

**Note:** Some games could reasonably fit multiple categories; this taxonomy prioritizes their primary mechanic.
